## What it is

The System and Information Integrity policy states what the organization requires for system and information integrity and who is accountable for it. It meets [SI-1](/controls/si/si-1/) through the sections every family policy shares, and adds one statement group per control. Each baseline variant includes only the controls in that baseline, taken from the NIST SP 800-53B profiles.

Adopt the ready-to-adopt edition: fill every highlighted field, delete any "Federal systems" section that does not apply, and have the accountable official approve it. The annotated edition adds guidance on why each section exists and what assessors look for.

## Decisions to make first

The policy has 92 organization-defined parameters across all variants; each appears as a highlighted field with its typical value where one is given. Settle these first:

| Decision | Controls | Typical | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who installs updates for each kind of component, and how are urgent updates approved? | [SI-2](/controls/si/si-2/), [SI-2(2)](/controls/si/si-2/#si-2.2) | The IT operations team patches operating systems and common software monthly as standard changes; application teams update their own code and libraries; updates for known exploited vulnerabilities go through the emergency change process. | Chief Information Security Officer, with the change control board |
| Where do monitoring data and alerts go, and who triages them, at what hours? | [SI-4](/controls/si/si-4/), [SI-4(2)](/controls/si/si-4/#si-4.2), [SI-4(5)](/controls/si/si-4/#si-4.5) | A central security information and event management (SIEM) platform, triaged around the clock by the security operations team or a managed security service. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Which malicious code, spam and monitoring protections are common controls, and which does each system own? | [SI-3](/controls/si/si-3/), [SI-4](/controls/si/si-4/), [SI-8](/controls/si/si-8/) | Endpoint detection and response, the email gateway and the SIEM platform are common controls; each system owner makes sure every component runs the agent and sends its logs, and owns application-specific detections. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Is encrypted traffic decrypted for inspection, and which categories are exempt? | [SI-4(10)](/controls/si/si-4/#si-4.10) | Decrypted at the internet boundary proxy, with health, financial and similar personal categories exempt, as approved by legal counsel and the senior privacy official. | Chief Information Security Officer, with legal counsel and the senior privacy official |
| Where are retention periods set for each type of information, and who confirms information is disposed of at the end? | [SI-12](/controls/si/si-12/), [SI-12(3)](/controls/si/si-12/#si-12.3) | In the organization's records retention schedule, owned by records management; each system security plan and privacy impact assessment names the periods that apply, and the system owner confirms disposal each year. | System owner, with records management |

Record your values in the [System and Information Integrity decision worksheet](/templates/worksheets/si/), which lists every parameter with its typical value.

## Preview (Moderate baseline, annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
The sections before and after Policy statements meet SI-1, which asks for a policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination and compliance, plus procedures, dissemination, a designated official and a review cycle. Assessors check each element, so keep every section even when it is short. Each statement cites the SI-1 item it meets. If you adopt several family policies, the same sections repeat in each; that is expected, and it lets each policy stand alone.
:::

### Purpose

This policy states what <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> requires for System and Information Integrity, and who is accountable for meeting those requirements. (SI-1a.1(a))

### Scope

This policy applies at the <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level</span> to every system that <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> owns or operates, or that is operated on its behalf, and to every person with access to those systems, including employees, contractors and partners. (SI-1a.1(a))

### Roles and responsibilities

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is accountable for this policy and shall approve exceptions to it. (SI-1a.1(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the system and information integrity policy and procedures</span> shall manage the development, documentation and dissemination of this policy and its procedures. (SI-1b)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement this policy for their system and document how in the system security plan. (SI-1a.1(a))
- Each person within scope shall follow this policy and report suspected violations to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>. (SI-1a.1(a))

### Management commitment

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> approves this policy and shall provide the resources needed to implement it. (SI-1a.1(a))

### Coordination

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate this policy with the legal, privacy, human resources and procurement functions, and with the owners of related policies, before each approval. (SI-1a.1(a))

### Compliance

- This policy shall be consistent with the laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards and guidelines that apply to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>, including <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: laws, regulations and standards that apply to the organization</span>. (SI-1a.1(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review compliance with this policy through the organization's assessment and continuous monitoring activities. (SI-1a.1(a))
- An exception to this policy shall be requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with its compensating measures. (SI-1a.1(a))
- Violations of this policy shall be handled through the organization's sanctions process. (SI-1a.1(a))

### Procedures

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the system and information integrity policy and procedures</span> shall ensure that documented procedures exist to implement this policy and its associated controls. (SI-1a.2)

### Dissemination

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the system and information integrity policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the system and information integrity policy is to be disseminated</span>. (SI-1a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the system and information integrity policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate the procedures that implement this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the system and information integrity procedures are to be disseminated</span>. (SI-1a)

### Policy statements

:::note[Guidance]
Each statement below comes from the clause for one control or enhancement in the chosen baseline. The reference at the end of each statement names the control item it meets.
:::

#### Flaw remediation (SI-2)

:::note[Guidance]
SI-2 is the fixing half of vulnerability management: RA-5 finds the flaws, and SI-2 installs the updates that correct them. The installation times here count from the release of the update, while the RA-5 remediation times count from when a finding is reported, so keep the two sets of values consistent. The [Patch and Flaw Remediation Standard](/templates/standards/patch-and-flaw-remediation-standard/) sets the test groups, deployment rings and schedules. NIST SP 800-40 Rev. 4, Guide to Enterprise Patch Management Planning (April 2022, current as of September 2026), describes how to plan patching as routine preventive maintenance.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall identify system flaws from vulnerability scanning and monitoring, vendor security advisories, assessments and incident analysis. (SI-2a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall report identified flaws that affect the system to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> and record each in the system's flaw tracking. (SI-2a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall correct identified system flaws. (SI-2a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall test software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness and potential side effects before installing them in production. (SI-2b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall install security-relevant software and firmware updates within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to install security-relevant software updates after the release of the updates <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: known exploited: as soon as possible, within days; critical and high: 30 days; moderate: 90 days; low: 180 days</span></span> of the release of the updates. (SI-2c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall enter any security-relevant update that cannot be installed in time in the system's plan of action and milestones, with a planned date and any compensating measures, before its installation time ends. (SI-2c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall incorporate flaw remediation into the organization's configuration management process, recording routine updates as standard changes and urgent updates as emergency changes. (SI-2d)

:::note[Guidance]
Unsupported software and firmware cannot be fixed. Record each unsupported component as a flaw, with a replacement date in the plan of action and milestones, until it is removed (SA-22).
:::

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

CISA [BOD 26-04](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/bod-26-04-prioritizing-security-updates-based-risk), Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (June 10, 2026), sets remediation deadlines for federal civilian agencies by whether an asset is publicly exposed, whether the vulnerability is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, whether exploitation can be automated, and its technical impact, from 3 days to "fix on system upgrade". Its clock starts when CISA adds a vulnerability to the KEV catalog or the agency identifies it, whichever is first. It revoked BOD 22-01 and BOD 19-02. It does not apply to national security systems. As of September 2026.

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall set the SI-2c installation times no longer than the deadlines CISA BOD 26-04 sets, and install security updates within those deadlines. (SI-2c)

</div>

#### Automated flaw remediation status (SI-2(2))

:::note[Guidance]
Patch compliance reports from the patch management tool, checked against authenticated vulnerability scans, show which components are missing updates. Components the tools cannot reach, such as appliances, need a manual check on the same schedule.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall determine whether system components have applicable security-relevant software and firmware updates installed, using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms to determine if applicable security-relevant software and firmware updates are installed on system components <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the patch management and vulnerability scanning tools</span></span>, <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to determine if applicable security-relevant software and firmware updates are installed on system components <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least weekly</span></span>. (SI-2(2))

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

CISA [BOD 23-01](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/bod-23-01-improving-asset-visibility-and-vulnerability-detection-federal-networks), Improving Asset Visibility and Vulnerability Detection on Federal Networks (October 3, 2022), requires federal civilian agencies to perform automated asset discovery every 7 days and to initiate vulnerability enumeration across all discovered assets, including roaming devices such as laptops, every 14 days. As of September 2026.

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system's assets are covered by automated asset discovery at least every 7 days and by vulnerability enumeration at least every 14 days, as CISA BOD 23-01 requires. (SI-2(2))

</div>

#### Malicious code protection (SI-3)

:::note[Guidance]
Endpoint detection and response on servers and workstations, together with malware scanning in the email and web gateways, usually covers system entry and exit points. Non-signature-based means behavior or reputation analysis, which catches malware no signature yet describes. Enterprise tools are often common controls; the system owner makes sure every component that can run an agent has one.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: signature-based; non-signature-based <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: signature-based and non-signature-based</span></span> malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code. (SI-3a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure malicious code protection mechanisms update automatically as new releases are available, in accordance with the organization's configuration management policy and procedures. (SI-3b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall configure malicious code protection mechanisms to perform periodic scans of the system <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which malicious code protection mechanisms perform scans <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least weekly</span></span>. (SI-3c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall configure malicious code protection mechanisms to perform real-time scans of files from external sources at <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: endpoint; network entry and exit points <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: endpoint and network entry and exit points</span></span> as the files are downloaded, opened or executed. (SI-3c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall configure malicious code protection mechanisms to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: block malicious code; quarantine malicious code; take [Assignment: organization-defined action] <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: block and quarantine malicious code</span></span> and to send an alert to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to be alerted when malicious code is detected <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the security operations team</span></span> when malicious code is detected. (SI-3c.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall review reported false positives, approve any scan exclusion with a documented reason and an expiry date, and record the effect of false positives on the availability of the system. (SI-3d)

#### System monitoring (SI-4)

:::note[Guidance]
System monitoring takes in the audit records reviewed under AU-6 and adds endpoint, network and cloud detection. The [System Monitoring Standard](/templates/standards/system-monitoring-standard/) sets the log sources, detection coverage, alert handling and reporting. Legal review of monitoring (SI-4f) is usually done once for the organization's monitoring program and repeated when monitoring changes, with a system use notification under AC-8.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall monitor the system to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks in accordance with the following monitoring objectives: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: monitoring objectives to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks on the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: detecting attacks, malware, unauthorized access, privilege misuse and data exfiltration</span></span>. (SI-4a.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall monitor the system to detect unauthorized local, network and remote connections. (SI-4a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall identify unauthorized use of the system through <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: techniques and methods used to identify unauthorized use of the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: log correlation in the security information and event management (SIEM) platform, endpoint detection and response, network intrusion detection and user behavior analytics</span></span>. (SI-4b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure monitoring capabilities are deployed strategically within the system to collect the essential information the monitoring objectives call for, including at the managed interfaces under SC-7. (SI-4c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure monitoring capabilities can be deployed at ad hoc locations within the system to track specific types of transactions of interest to the organization. (SI-4c.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall analyze detected events and anomalies, and refer suspected incidents to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span>. (SI-4d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall adjust the level of system monitoring activity when there is a change in risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations or the Nation. (SI-4e)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall obtain a legal opinion on system monitoring activities before they begin and whenever they change significantly. (SI-4f)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall provide <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: system monitoring information to be provided to personnel or roles <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: alerts and monitoring reports</span></span> to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom system monitoring information is to be provided <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner and the incident response team</span></span>, <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: as needed; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: as needed, and at least monthly</span></span>. (SI-4g)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

[OMB M-26-14](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/M-26-14-Ensuring-Effective-and-Efficient-Agency-Logging-and-Network-Visibility-to-Defend-Against-Evolving-Cyber-Threats.pdf), Ensuring Effective and Efficient Agency Logging and Network Visibility to Defend Against Evolving Cyber Threats (May 22, 2026), rescinded M-21-31. It directs agencies to prioritize two logging objectives, continuous event monitoring and threat hunting, investigation, response and forensics, for all information systems owned or operated by the agency or by third parties on its behalf, and to adhere to CISA's [Logging Reference Architecture](https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/logging-reference-architecture) (published August 20, 2026). Its Appendix B requires logs that support monitoring for suspicious activity identified by security tooling, known indicators of compromise and anomalous system or user activity, with automated alerts, and that are readily available to the agency's top-level security operations center. It does not apply to national security systems. As of September 2026.

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system's logs are readily available to the agency's top-level security operations center, as OMB M-26-14 requires. (SI-4c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall use the system's logs to monitor for suspicious activity identified by security tooling, known indicators of compromise and anomalous system or user activity, and generate automated alerts for them, as OMB M-26-14 Appendix B requires. (SI-4a.1)
- In the event of a known or suspected compromise, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall provide logs and other relevant data to CISA and the FBI on request, to the extent consistent with applicable law, as OMB M-26-14 requires. (SI-4g)

</div>

#### Automated tools and mechanisms for real-time analysis (SI-4(2))

:::note[Guidance]
Correlation rules and analytics in the SIEM, and the detection engines in endpoint and network tools, are the automated tools. Near real-time means minutes, not the next day's review.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall employ automated tools and mechanisms, such as correlation rules in the SIEM platform and endpoint detection and response, to support near real-time analysis of events. (SI-4(2))

#### Inbound and outbound communications traffic (SI-4(4))

:::note[Guidance]
Outbound monitoring is where data exfiltration and command-and-control traffic show up. Threat intelligence feeds supply the known malicious sources and destinations; a baseline of normal volumes supplies the unusual ones.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall determine and document criteria for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions for inbound and outbound communications traffic. (SI-4(4)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall monitor inbound communications traffic <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to monitor inbound communications traffic for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: continuously</span></span> for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions that are to be monitored in inbound communications traffic <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: connections from known malicious sources, unapproved protocols and ports, and scanning or password-guessing patterns</span></span>. (SI-4(4)(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall monitor outbound communications traffic <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to monitor outbound communications traffic for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: continuously</span></span> for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions that are to be monitored in outbound communications traffic <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: connections to known malicious destinations, unusual data volumes, unapproved protocols and regular beaconing to external hosts</span></span>. (SI-4(4)(b))

#### System-generated alerts (SI-4(5))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system alerts <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to be alerted when indications of compromise or potential compromise occur <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the security operations team</span></span> when the following system-generated indications of compromise or potential compromise occur: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: compromise indicators <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: indicators of compromise from the detection tools and threat intelligence feeds</span></span>. (SI-4(5))

#### Security alerts, advisories and directives (SI-5)

:::note[Guidance]
Subscribing to the CISA advisories and the vendor security bulletins for every product in the component inventory (CM-8) is the usual starting point. The value is in routing: each alert reaches the people who run the affected component, with a due date.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall receive system security alerts, advisories and directives from <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: external organizations from whom system security alerts, advisories, and directives are to be received on an ongoing basis <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: CISA, the vendors of the system's components, and the organization's information sharing and analysis center</span></span> on an ongoing basis. (SI-5a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall generate internal security alerts, advisories and directives as deemed necessary. (SI-5b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall disseminate security alerts, advisories and directives to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]; [Assignment: organization-defined elements]; [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations] <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: system owners and system administrators, the security operations and incident response teams, and the service providers who operate systems for the organization, where an alert affects them</span></span>. (SI-5c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement security directives in accordance with their established time frames, or notify the issuing organization of the degree of noncompliance. (SI-5d)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

The Federal Information Security Modernization Act requires the head of each agency to comply with the binding operational directives and emergency directives the Secretary of Homeland Security issues under 44 U.S.C. § 3553(b) and (h) ([44 U.S.C. § 3554(a)(1)(B)(ii) and (v)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim)). CISA publishes them on its [Cybersecurity Directives](https://www.cisa.gov/directives) page; they do not apply to national security systems. As of September 2026.

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall track each CISA binding operational directive and emergency directive that applies to the agency, and ensure system owners complete its required actions and reports within the time frames it sets. (SI-5d)

</div>

#### Software, firmware and information integrity (SI-7)

:::note[Guidance]
File integrity monitoring, signed and verified container images, secure boot and measured boot are the usual integrity verification tools. Changes approved under CM-3 are expected; integrity verification finds the ones that were not.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to the following software: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: software requiring integrity verification tools to be employed to detect unauthorized changes <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: operating system files, installed applications, container images and security tool binaries</span></span>. (SI-7a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to the following firmware: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: firmware requiring integrity verification tools to be employed to detect unauthorized changes <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: server, network device and endpoint firmware and boot components, where the platform supports verification</span></span>. (SI-7a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to the following information: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information requiring integrity verification tools to be employed to detect unauthorized changes <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: security configuration files, audit logs, and the critical data stores named in the system security plan</span></span>. (SI-7a)
- When unauthorized changes to software are detected, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: actions to be taken when unauthorized changes to software are detected <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: alert the security operations team, restore the approved version, and handle an unauthorized change as a suspected incident</span></span>. (SI-7b)
- When unauthorized changes to firmware are detected, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: actions to be taken when unauthorized changes to firmware are detected <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: alert the security operations team, restore the approved firmware, and handle an unauthorized change as a suspected incident</span></span>. (SI-7b)
- When unauthorized changes to information are detected, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: actions to be taken when unauthorized changes to information are detected <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: alert the security operations team and the information owner, restore the information from a trusted source or backup, and handle an unauthorized change as a suspected incident</span></span>. (SI-7b)

#### Integrity checks (SI-7(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall perform an integrity check of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: software on which an integrity check is to be performed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the software named for integrity verification under SI-7</span></span> <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: at startup; at [Assignment: organization-defined transitional states or security-relevant events]; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at startup, after each update or change to the software, and at least weekly</span></span>. (SI-7(1))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall perform an integrity check of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: firmware on which an integrity check is to be performed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the firmware named for integrity verification under SI-7</span></span> <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: at startup; at [Assignment: organization-defined transitional states or security-relevant events]; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at startup, after each firmware update, and at least monthly</span></span>. (SI-7(1))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall perform an integrity check of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information on which an integrity check is to be performed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the information named for integrity verification under SI-7</span></span> <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: at startup; at [Assignment: organization-defined transitional states or security-relevant events]; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: after each authorized change to the information, and at least daily</span></span>. (SI-7(1))

#### Integration of detection and response (SI-7(7))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall incorporate the detection of the following unauthorized changes into the organization's incident response capability: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: security-relevant changes to the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: unauthorized changes to operating system and application files, security configuration settings, firmware and audit logging settings</span></span>. (SI-7(7))

#### Spam protection (SI-8)

:::note[Guidance]
Spam protection sits in the email gateway or the cloud email service's filtering, and in some cases in web or messaging gateways. Publishing SPF, DKIM and DMARC records for the organization's own domains helps other organizations reject mail that spoofs them.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall employ spam protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and act on unsolicited messages. (SI-8a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall update spam protection mechanisms when new releases are available, in accordance with the organization's configuration management policy and procedures. (SI-8b)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

CISA [BOD 18-01](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/bod-18-01-enhance-email-and-web-security), Enhance Email and Web Security (October 16, 2017), requires federal civilian agencies to have valid SPF and DMARC records for all second-level agency domains, to set a DMARC policy of "reject" for all second-level domains and mail-sending hosts, and to add the address the directive designates (`reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov`) as a recipient of DMARC aggregate reports. As of September 2026.

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure each second-level domain the system uses has valid SPF and DMARC records, with a DMARC policy of reject for the domain and its mail-sending hosts, as CISA BOD 18-01 requires. (SI-8a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall include `reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov` as a recipient of the domain's DMARC aggregate reports, as CISA BOD 18-01 requires. (SI-8a)

</div>

#### Automatic updates (SI-8(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure spam protection mechanisms are updated automatically <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to automatically update spam protection mechanisms <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: as the vendor releases updates, and at least daily</span></span>. (SI-8(2))

#### Information input validation (SI-10)

:::note[Guidance]
Validate on the server, against an allow list of expected type, length, format and range, and keep data separate from commands (for example, parameterized database queries). Code review and application security testing (SA-11) are where assessors look for evidence.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system checks the validity of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information inputs to the system requiring validity checks <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: all inputs from users, external systems and interfaces, including web forms, API requests, file uploads and query parameters</span></span>. (SI-10)

#### Error handling (SI-11)

:::note[Guidance]
Users see a short message and a reference number; the detail, such as stack traces, database errors and internal paths, goes to the logs. Login and password reset messages should not reveal whether an account exists.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system generates error messages that provide the information needed for corrective action without revealing information that could be exploited. (SI-11a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system reveals detailed error messages only to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom error messages are to be revealed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: system administrators and developers with a need to know, through the system's logs</span></span>. (SI-11b)

#### Information management and retention (SI-12)

:::note[Guidance]
Retention applies to everything the system holds or produces: records, logs, backups, reports and exports. Records management usually owns the retention schedule; the system owner makes the system follow it, including deletion at the end of the period. For personally identifiable information, the retention periods also go in the privacy impact assessment.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall manage and retain information within the system, and information output from the system, in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, guidelines and operational requirements. (SI-12)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall document the retention period and the authority for it for each type of information the system holds, drawn from the organization's records retention schedule. (SI-12)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall dispose of information when its retention period ends, unless a legal hold or an approved extension applies. (SI-12)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

The head of each federal agency must "make and preserve records containing adequate and proper documentation" of the agency's functions ([44 U.S.C. § 3101](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3101&num=0&edition=prelim)), and federal records "may not be alienated or destroyed" except under chapter 33 of title 44 ([44 U.S.C. § 3314](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3314&num=0&edition=prelim)): that is, under records schedules approved by the Archivist of the United States, including the General Records Schedules the Archivist issues for records common to several or all agencies ([44 U.S.C. § 3303a(d)](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3303a&num=0&edition=prelim)). As of September 2026.

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall retain and dispose of federal records in the system only as an approved agency records schedule or a General Records Schedule allows. (SI-12)

</div>

#### Memory protection (SI-16)

:::note[Guidance]
Modern operating systems provide these protections by default; the evidence is a configuration baseline (CM-6) that keeps them enabled and a scan that shows no exceptions.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement the following controls to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: controls to be implemented to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: data execution prevention and address space layout randomization, enforced by the operating system and hardware</span></span>. (SI-16)

### Review and update

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the system and information integrity policy and procedures</span> shall review and update this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current system and information integrity policy is reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require the current system and information integrity policy to be reviewed and updated</span>. (SI-1c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the system and information integrity policy and procedures</span> shall review and update the procedures that implement this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current system and information integrity procedures are reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require the system and information integrity procedures to be reviewed and updated</span>. (SI-1c.2)

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

For federal information systems, this policy also carries out the agency's information security responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 ([44 U.S.C. § 3554](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim), Federal agency responsibilities) and [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf), Appendix I, Responsibilities for Protecting and Managing Federal Information Resources.

- Where the agency's organization-wide policy sets a value for a parameter in this policy, each system shall use that value or a stricter one. (SI-1a.1(b))

</div>
